interface.title: NPLinker Webapp
interface.field: Natural product discovery / microbial genome mining paired with metabolomics
interface.stage_of_work: Looking at results after the NPLinker Python API has already computed and scored links between gene clusters and metabolites, and choosing which ones to follow up
interface.what_it_is_for: Load an NPLinker result pickle whose links were already computed with the NPLinker Python API. Get an overview of gene cluster families (GCFs) and molecular families (MFs), choose a link direction (GCF→MF or MF→GCF), and filter and select GCFs or MFs. Pull up the precomputed links that were made with a chosen method (Metcalf), RAW/STANDARDISED setting and cutoff; the webapp does not compute or re-threshold scores. Then sort, filter, choose columns for and export the Candidate Links table.

data.note: Load Demo Data hung on its spinner with nothing loaded (screens/002.webp, 003.webp), because the server has no network. I used the uploader instead (the 'Import Data' box, not the 'drag and drop or select a file' label in the notes) with mock_obj_data.pkl: 5 GCFs, 5 MFs, with links (screens/005.webp, 006.webp). Later I uploaded mock_obj_data_no_links.pkl to test a result without computed links (screens/052.webp–055.webp). Two Excel files were downloaded: nplinker_genom_to_metabol.xlsx (10.5 KB; 12,064 bytes in the replay) and nplinker_metabol_to_genom.xlsx. The reader can only report their size because they are binary, so I could not check what is in them.

features.name: OR-combined multi-row ID/category filter builder
features.general: Build a filter from several rows, each choosing a field type (ID list or category multi-select). Rows are joined with OR and applied in one step to a selectable table.
features.specific: Genomics filter: + adds a row labelled OR. Each row is GCF ID (comma list) or BGC Class (multi-select whose vocabulary follows MIBiG < 4.0 or ≥ 4.0). Apply Filters reduces the GCF Data table. The Metabolomics filter does the same with MF ID or Spectrum ID.
steps: pick the field type for the row (GCF ID / BGC Class, or MF ID / Spectrum ID)
type a comma-separated ID list or pick categories
press + to add another OR row
optionally switch the class vocabulary (MIBiG version), which clears picked classes
press Apply Filters and read Total rows
serves_tasks: Narrow the list by ID or by category

features.name: Selectable data table feeding a stored-link lookup
features.general: Tick rows (or select all) in a filtered table, name the scoring method, normalisation and minimum cutoff that the precomputed links were made with, then pull up the stored links for only those rows. Nothing is computed and scores are not thresholded. A warning shows when no stored link set matches, or when the file holds no links.
features.specific: Tick GCF or MF rows (Selected rows counter). In Scoring choose RAW or STANDARDISED, Metcalf and a cutoff (>=), then press Show Results. It fills Candidate Links with links whose stored method, standardised flag and computation cutoff match (stored cutoff ≥ entered value). It shows 'No matching links found for selected GCFs.' when no stored set matches, or 'No processed links available.' for a file without links.
steps: tick rows or the header select-all box
expand Scoring and choose RAW or STANDARDISED to match how the links were computed
choose the method (Metcalf) and enter a cutoff no higher than the one used in the NPLinker API
press Show Results
read Candidate Links or the warning banner
serves_tasks: Pick the items to look up links for
Retrieve the precomputed link scores for the chosen items, naming the scoring method and settings they were computed with
Load a result that has no computed links

features.name: Results grid with expression filters, sort, column chooser and Excel export
features.general: A results table where each column takes a filter expression (such as '> 35' or a value), columns sort by clicking, a modal toggles extra annotation columns, and the table exports to a spreadsheet.
features.specific: Candidate Links table: the filter data... row takes expressions such as '> 35'. The header sort arrow sorts. Columns settings switches on Top Spectrum MF ID, Top Spectrum Precursor m/z, Top Spectrum GNPS ID, Top Spectrum Score, MiBIG IDs, BGC Classes (or Top GCF columns such as Top GCF BGC Classes and Top GCF Score on the MF→GCF tab). Download Results (Excel) saves an .xlsx with 'Best Candidate Links' and 'All Candidate Links' sheets (per the source code; the run could not open the file).
steps: type an expression in a column's filter cell and press Enter
click a header sort arrow
open Columns settings and switch columns on or off, then Close
press Download Results (Excel)
serves_tasks: Keep only high-confidence links with a threshold expression
Order the results by a score
Show annotation columns next to each link to form hypotheses

features.name: Overview histogram with switchable grouping
features.general: A bar chart counting items, grouped by a field picked from a dropdown, with hover tooltips listing the item IDs in each bar
features.specific: Select X-axis (# BGCs or BGC Classes) re-draws the # GCFs bar chart. Hovering a bar lists its GCF IDs. Plotly toolbar offers zoom, pan, box/lasso select and PNG download. Clicking a bar does not filter the table.
steps: choose the grouping in Select X-axis
hover a bar to read the IDs in it
optionally use the toolbar to zoom or save a PNG
serves_tasks: See how many items there are and how they break down by category

features.name: Uploader with load status
features.general: Upload a saved analysis file and see its name and size confirmed. Loading a new file resets every view.
features.specific: Import Data box accepts an NPLinker pickle and shows 'Successfully uploaded: <name> [size]'. Uploading another file resets tabs, filters and selections. A Load Demo Data button fetches a sample (it failed here with no network).
steps: click Import Data (or drop a file)
pick the .pkl file
read the success line and check the tabs are enabled
serves_tasks: Load a saved analysis result into the tool
Load a result that has no computed links

features.name: Paired link-direction tabs
features.general: Two tabs read the same links from either side (A→B or B→A). Each tab has its own data table, filter, row selection, link lookup, results grid and export.
features.specific: The default genomics tab works on the GCF Data table and gives GCF→MF Candidate Links. The Metabolomics -> Genomics tab works on the MF Data table (# Spectra) with the Metabolomics filter (MF ID / Spectrum ID). Show Results there gives MF→GCF Candidate Links (Top GCF columns), and Download gives nplinker_metabol_to_genom.xlsx.
steps: pick the direction tab
filter and tick rows in that tab's Data table
press Show Results to fill that direction's Candidate Links
choose columns and download that direction's results
serves_tasks: Choose which direction to read the links: from gene clusters to metabolites, or from metabolites to gene clusters
Narrow the list by ID or by category
Pick the items to look up links for
Show annotation columns next to each link to form hypotheses

not_done: The Scoring cutoff is not a score threshold. With RAW cutoff 30 or 50, and with STANDARDISED cutoff 2, every Show Results said 'No matching links found for selected GCFs.' (screens/034.webp, 035.webp, 036.webp). This happened even though Top Spectrum Scores were 52–53; RAW cutoff 0 brought the links back (screens/037.webp). The reviewer read callbacks.py:1766-1775 and the README, which says links are computed in the NPLinker Python API. Show Results only picks precomputed links whose stored method, standardised flag and computation cutoff match (stored cutoff ≥ entered value). It never compares the score itself, so only RAW cutoff 0 matched the links in this file. To keep only high scores, use a column filter expression such as '> 35'

Did not read the Excel files' contents: the download reader reports only size for binary files (10.5 KB for the GCF→MF file). The reviewer's reading of callbacks.py:2350, 2471 says each file has 'Best Candidate Links' and 'All Candidate Links' sheets; no screen shows this
